Aim for recurring clients, not just more clients

Cleaning is one of the few home services people buy on a schedule. One weekly or biweekly client is worth many one-time jobs, and a schedule full of regulars is easier to staff and route. So every channel below is about two things: getting the first clean, and turning it into a standing appointment.

1. Show up when people search "house cleaning near me"

Most new cleaning clients start on Google, usually on their phone. Make sure your Google Business Profile is verified, uses "House cleaning service" (or your most specific category) as the primary category, and lists the towns you serve. Add real photos of finished rooms. Then put a page behind it that answers the questions people have before booking a cleaner:

  • Which towns do you cover?
  • What's included in a standard clean versus a deep clean?
  • Do you bring your own supplies? Are you insured?
  • How do I get a quote?
An Enoma page answers those in one screen, with a quote form that sends requests straight to you and a tap-to-call button. See your page in 30 seconds, built from your Google listing.

2. Build clusters, not a scattered map

Drive time eats cleaning margins. A client next door to an existing client is worth more than one across town. When you finish at a home, leave a card or door hanger with two or three neighbors. Ask regulars if anyone on their street has asked about a cleaner. Clusters let you fit more homes into a day.

3. Ask for referrals at the moment clients are happiest

Right after a great clean, especially the first one, ask: "If you know anyone who'd like this every couple of weeks, we have openings on your street on Thursdays." Specific openings feel real. A small thank-you for referrals, such as a discount on their next clean, is a common and fair way to encourage them.

4. Turn first cleans into standing appointments

Many first-time clients book a deep clean and never think about what's next. Make the next step easy:

  • Offer a recurring rate that's clearly lower than the one-time price.
  • Book the next visit before you leave: "Want me to put you down for two weeks from today?"
  • Follow up by text a few days later if they didn't book.

5. Collect reviews from every regular

People are letting a stranger into their home, so trust decides the booking. Reviews that mention reliability and the same cleaner each time are gold. Text your review link after the second or third visit, when the client already knows you're consistent. Here's how to ask for Google reviews, including what not to do.

6. Pick a few local channels and do them well

Neighborhood Facebook groups, Nextdoor, local parents' groups and realtors (move-out and move-in cleans) can all work. Don't try all of them. Pick two, show up consistently, and always point people to the same page with your towns and quote form.

Common questions

How to get more cleaning clients who stay every month: common questions

How do I get my first cleaning clients?

Start with your Google Business Profile and a simple page listing your towns, services and a quote form, then tell everyone you know and post in neighborhood groups. Leave cards with neighbors of every home you clean, and ask happy clients for referrals and Google reviews from the start.

How do I get recurring cleaning clients instead of one-time jobs?

Offer a lower recurring rate than your one-time price, book the next visit before you leave the first clean, and follow up by text if they didn't book. Reliability, the same cleaner each visit, and reviews that mention both make clients stay.

Where do people look for house cleaners?

Mostly Google ("house cleaning near me" on a phone), referrals from friends and neighbors, and local Facebook or Nextdoor groups. All of them work better when they point to one page that shows your towns, what's included and how to get a quote.

Do cleaning businesses need a website?

It helps. People want to check your services, coverage area and reviews before letting you into their home. One clear page with a quote form and your Google rating does the job for most small cleaning businesses.
